sn4.23:4.4: A rather curious epithet for Mara to use. It is identical with “Lucifer”. http://www.etymonline.com/index.php?term=lucifer
sn4.23:10.7:
The
 “arched harp” (_vīṇa_) was a multi-stringed instrument held in the lap,
 with the strings attached across a curved open arch or bow. It is not 
the modern Indian instrument called veena, which is a lute or stick 
zither. Pañcasikha’s harp is described in the same way ([dn21:1.2.4]()), and tradition says they were in fact the same instrument.
